audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Hezekiah reform, Assyrian conquest, tribute, Jerusalem delegation, and Rabshakeh propaganda narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for centralized religious reform, bronze-serpent destruction, Philistine campaign, Samaria deportation recap, Sennacherib's conquest of Judah, temple stripping for tribute, siege delegation, multilingual propaganda, bodily humiliation threats, deceptive resettlement promises, and civilian silence.

verses.restored: In third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz king of Judah became king.
Twenty-five years old was he when he became king, and twenty-nine years he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Abi daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right in eyes of YHWH, according to all David his father had done.

He removed high places, broke pillars, cut down Asherah, and shattered bronze serpent Moses had made, for until those days children of Israel burned incense to it; he called it Nehushtan, a bronze thing.
In YHWH Divine of Israel he trusted; after him there was none like him among all kings of Judah, nor among those before him.
He clung to YHWH and did not turn from following him, but kept commandments YHWH commanded Moses.
YHWH was with him; wherever he went he acted wisely/prospered. He rebelled against king of Assyria and did not serve him.
He struck Philistines as far as Gaza and its borders, from watchtower to fortified city.
In fourth year of king Hezekiah, seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria went up against Samaria and besieged it.
At end of three years they captured it. In sixth year of Hezekiah, ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was captured.
King of Assyria exiled Israel to Assyria and settled them in Halah, Habor by river Gozan, and cities of Medes.
Because they did not listen to voice of YHWH their Divine but transgressed his covenant—all Moses servant of YHWH commanded—they neither listened nor did.
In fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria went up against all fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

Hezekiah king of Judah sent to king of Assyria at Lachish, saying, I have sinned; turn from me. Whatever you place upon me I will bear. King of Assyria imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
Hezekiah gave all silver found in house of YHWH and treasuries of king's house.
At that time Hezekiah cut gold from doors of temple of YHWH and doorposts Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and gave it to king of Assyria.

King of Assyria sent Tartan, Rab-saris, and Rabshakeh from Lachish to king Hezekiah with a heavy force against Jerusalem. They went up, came to Jerusalem, and stood by conduit of upper pool on highway of Fuller's Field.
They called to king, and Eliakim son of Hilkiah over house, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder went out to them.
Rabshakeh said to them, Say now to Hezekiah, Thus says great king, king of Assyria: What is this trust in which you trust?
You say, Only a word of lips is counsel and strength for war. Now upon whom do you trust that you rebel against me?
Now look, you trust in staff of this crushed reed, Egypt, which if a man leans upon it enters his palm and pierces it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust in him.
But if you say to me, In YHWH our Divine we trust—is he not the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, Before this altar in Jerusalem you shall bow?
Now please make a wager with my lord king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able to give riders for them.
How then can you turn back face of one governor among least servants of my lord, while you trust in Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
Now have I gone up apart from YHWH against this place to destroy it? YHWH said to me, Go up against this land and destroy it.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, Shebna, and Joah said to Rabshakeh, Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand; do not speak with us in Judean in ears of people upon wall.
Rabshakeh said to them, Has my lord sent me to your lord and to you to speak these words? Is it not to men sitting upon wall, who will eat their own excrement and drink their own urine with you?
Rabshakeh stood and called with great voice in Judean, spoke and said, Hear word of great king, king of Assyria.
Thus says king: Let Hezekiah not deceive you, for he is not able to deliver you from his hand.
Let Hezekiah not make you trust in YHWH, saying, Delivering, YHWH will deliver us, and this city shall not be given into hand of king of Assyria.
Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says king of Assyria: Make blessing/treaty with me and come out to me, and each shall eat from his vine and fig tree and drink water of his cistern,

until I come and take you to a land like your land, a land of grain and new wine, bread and vineyards, olive oil and honey, that you may live and not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah when he entices you, saying, YHWH will deliver us.
Have gods of nations delivered, each his land, from hand of king of Assyria?
Where are gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah? Did they deliver Samaria from my hand?
Who among all gods of lands delivered their land from my hand, that YHWH should deliver Jerusalem from my hand?
People were silent and did not answer him a word, for command of king was, saying, Do not answer him.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah over house, Shebna the scribe, and Joah son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with garments torn and told him words of Rabshakeh.

translation_notes: Hezekiah's reform includes destruction of local shrines and a revered bronze object. Reform may challenge exploitative institutions, but this text cannot authorize attacks on living religious communities or cultural heritage.
The bronze serpent is reduced to 'a bronze thing' because an old liberation symbol has become an object of cult. The critique concerns how symbols function, not a blanket ban on sacred art.
Hezekiah's campaign against Philistine cities and rebellion against Assyria remain military and imperial actions; positive royal evaluation does not erase conquered civilians.
The recap of Samaria's fall uses covenant theology but must preserve Assyria's siege and deportation as imperial violence.
Sennacherib captures Judah's fortified cities before Jerusalem's crisis. The displaced, killed, taxed, and besieged population extends far beyond the capital narrative.
Hezekiah strips temple doors and treasury to pay tribute. Sacred wealth cannot guarantee security, and rulers may transfer communal resources under coercion.
Rabshakeh uses accurate critique, exaggeration, humiliation, religious claims, bodily terror, economic promise, and public-language strategy as siege propaganda.
The threat of eating excrement and drinking urine describes siege starvation and is intended to terrify civilians. It must not be sensationalized or used as degrading humor.
Assyria's promise of vines, cisterns, and a similar land disguises forced deportation as benevolent relocation.
Rabshakeh claims YHWH authorized the invasion. Claims of Divine military permission require moral scrutiny and may never be treated as self-authenticating.
The people's silence is disciplined crisis response under royal command, not consent or proof that they were unafraid.
safety_note: Do not use Hezekiah's reform to justify religious vandalism, erase Philistine civilians, blame Samarian exiles, celebrate temple stripping, or imitate siege propaganda. Center civilians hearing threats in their own language, communities already conquered, and the difference between promised relocation and forced deportation.
